title: Several Authorization values in one request
summary: Synthetic requests with two Authorization field lines (Basic, then Bearer) and with one line whose value joins a Basic and a Bearer credential with a comma.
rationale: A sender must not repeat a field that is not a list, and a recipient may combine lines, so the effective credential is not determined by the standard; a later line can even be deliberately misleading. Each value is still a credential-shaped token on its own line, so leaving any one unprotected may leak, but which is effective and whether the comma-joined form is two credentials is a parser policy question.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. RFC 9110 says a sender must not generate multiple lines of a field that does not allow list recombination and that duplicates can be misleading, but does not say which value governs. Candidate reading: all values as credentials. Header coalescing and parser policy are handed off to the owning repositories.

sources.supports: a sender MUST NOT generate multiple field lines with the same name ... unless that field's definition allows multiple field line values to be recombined as a comma-separated list
later field lines might include conditionals, authentication credentials, or deliberately misleading duplicate header fields

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
